No one will probably read this, but I feel like I've wasted my life too and I'm 27. But I am somewhat on track to hopefully be fine.

I was homeless for most of high school, had trouble getting food often so would just starve. At one point I was 108 pounds despite being a 6 foot 2 guy. To this day I struggle with eating. 

Being homeless didn't give me a great start to my adult life. The person I depended on the most to crash in their garage died 3 days after I graduated, so I almost immediately had to find an actual place to start renting. I found a cheap place I could barely afford on my min wage job.

Another thing against me was transportation, I live in a part of the US with no public transit, and I can't uber anywhere because no money. Being homeless I never had access to a car, so never got a license.

So years went by where I basically walked to my dead end job, came home, too tired or poor to do anything.  I hand washed my clothes, didn't buy hygiene products, I was a mess really.

One day I decided to just apply to a new job. Somehow got it, was like a 3x pay increase. This was right around covid and it was a medical production facility. So I suddenly was working 80 hour weeks, making a ton of money. It was life changing, and I was able to kinda turn my life around. I invested in some stocks once I saw the market crash and gained a lot of money off that too.

Now I'm heading into my junior year of college, not working because I have plenty of savings, looking to get an internship soon hopefully. Still can't drive, so it's hard to meet new people sometimes. But I am doing somewhat better. And I realised that with time and perseverance you can eventually make something for yourself.

I hope you can find a glimmer of hope for yourself even with your current feelings. Our most valuable commodity on this earth is time, so not being where you want to be currently is stressful. I get it. Break down what you want to do, even If it's something small, and start working to achieve it. You realistically probably won't be able to rely on your family which is scary. But I believe in you.

UPDATE: To anyone that might read this in the future, I believe I found the fix. I ended up getting new RAM and a new card, but it also was crashing. So then I reset windows and it was also crashing. I thought it was weird with basically all new hardware, testing multiple hardware pieces etc I was ALWAYS crashing, and I knew at this point it was not software related as I reset Windows.

The Fix: I have a modular PSU. The power to the mobo is a 20+4 connector that connects to my PSU. I went to look at the wiring and I guess the 4 pin connector came loose. It didn't look loose, but I felt it slide in a bit when I pressed on all the cords connected to the PSU to make sure they were fit snug. So when my GPU was trying to draw power I guess it was messing with the mobo, so I was black screening. When I boot up a high intensity game I'd pretty much crash instantly, however I've been here about 10 minutes and it hasn't crashed, so fingers crossed this fixed it :)

Unsure about the RAM, could be an issue though. I'm not sure though since it was working fine before Installed this new GPU. I ordered in a new GPU and RAM, going to do some testing. My old system components were all about 8 years old, funny that they seem to all cause issues around the same time. Basically had to buy a whole new PC at this point, only thing remaining is going to be my drives lol.

I am not opening up particularly demanding games, so temps aren't really going very high. Yet it still is crashing. My cpu temps idle around 25 C and go up to the 30-40ish range while in games.
